_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
He was wounded for our transgressions.
He was despised, and we held him of no account.
Upon him was the punishment that made us whole.
From the cross he cries, It is finished.
By his wounds we are healed.
Let us draw near in silence to the cross.
We behold the Lamb of God. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: On a hill outside the wall they lift him up between two thieves, and the sky goes dark over Jerusalem.
By his wounds we are healed.
He was despised and rejected, a man of sorrows, and we hid our faces from him.
By his wounds we are healed.
He was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that made us whole fell on him.
By his wounds we are healed.
From the dry ground of the cross he cries out, My God, why have you forsaken me, and then: It is finished.
By his wounds we are healed.
So let us draw near with confidence, through the curtain of his torn flesh, and worship.
By his wounds we are healed. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: They lift him up; the sky goes dark.
By his wounds we are healed.
Despised, rejected, a man of sorrows.
By his wounds we are healed.
He is wounded for our transgressions.
By his wounds we are healed.

By his wounds we are healed. Amen.
